model: Regulated utility dividend discount at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average, Q3 2026 10-Q EPS note: 2,202 basic + 78 as-converted 6.000% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred (converts Dec 2027) + ~5 equity awards = 2,285. Held FLAT in base and bull: the 10-Q states no equity issuance is expected through 2030 and SBC is already expensed inside earnings. The cover-page 2,680M includes ~478M shares held by the Utility and is not the outstanding count. The bear case's dilutive post-fire equity raise is carried as lower per-share earnings growth, not as a rising count.
inputs.sbc_source: PCG_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 (XBRL cash-flow add-back); EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0. Memo only on this route: the valued flow is the dividend out of earnings that are already after SBC expense.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.80 x 4.75% ERP = 8.95%, rounded to 9.0%. Beta 0.80 sits above the 0.65 used for investment-grade regulated peers in this folder (NI) for ordinary financial leverage: consolidated debt of $65.0B against $34.6B of equity, about $5.6B of it at the holding company, and sub-investment-grade holdco ratings. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios. Wildfire, legislative and CPUC risk is charged once, in the scenario paths (an explicit expected-disallowance haircut on earnings in base, a realised event in bear) and in the 30% bear weight, never as a rate premium on top.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease costs are inside the earnings stream; no lease liability is deducted because net debt is held at zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: Utility preferred stock ($252M NCI) is served before earnings to common, so it is charged once in the flow and not deducted again. The $1,579M mandatory convertible preferred is treated as converted (78M shares in the count), so its dividend is not deducted and its liquidation value is not subtracted.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. PG&E is a cost-of-service regulated electric and gas monopoly. The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row; its governing principle is to discount the flow the business actually produces at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues, and it warns that reported FCF is structurally negative for infrastructure in a capex supercycle without that being a signal. Reported FCF has been negative in 17 of the last 19 years (FY2025 -$3,071M on $11.8B capex against $4.6B of D&A) because rate base is being grown on purpose; an unlevered owner-FCF DCF would be a terminal value on a guessed capex normalisation minus $64B of debt. The flow that reaches shareholders is the dividend, funded by authorized returns on equity rate base, so the model capitalises dividends at the cost of equity through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero, the same route used for NEE and NI. ENGINE MAPPING. 'revenue' = non-GAAP core earnings to common (core EPS x the flat 2,285M diluted count). 'ebitda_margin' = the share of core earnings that is owner earnings: 100% less recurring non-core costs (Wildfire Fund expense, unrecoverable interest, legal and bankruptcy-era costs; GAAP EPS has run 13-20% below core every year since emergence, e.g. FY2025 $1.18 GAAP vs ~$1.50 core, 9M-2026 $1.06 GAAP) and less an expected wildfire-disallowance charge. 'capex_pct' = earnings retained to fund the equity share of rate-base growth, so margin minus capex_pct is the dividend payout on core earnings. D&A, tax, SBC and working capital are 0 because core earnings are already after all of them. FCF = dividends. CONSISTENCY RULE. Growth is tied to retention: per-share growth is approximately retention x earned ROE on book (diluted book value $15.13/share at 2026-09-30; FY2026 core EPS $1.65 = 10.9% on book, owner earnings ~9.3-9.6%), so the payout only rises as growth fades, and the terminal payout is the one that funds terminal growth. Without that link a 20% payout capitalised forever would understate value and a high payout with high growth would overstate it. FY0 CAVEAT. FY2025 core EPS is not in the 10-K (it is a press-release measure); $1.50 is backed out of the FY2026 guide of $1.64-1.66 described as about 10% growth, so year-1 growth of 10% lands exactly on the $1.65 midpoint. YEAR-1 TIMING. Year 1 is FY2026, of which $0.15 of the $0.20 dividend has already been paid; the full-period end-of-year discount on every flow more than offsets that. NET DEBT. Actual net debt is $64,124M (short-term $2,205M + current LTD $1,474M + LTD $61,347M, less cash $902M; $11.7B of it is non-recourse securitisation debt in VIEs); it is not deducted because the dividend is after interest. SBC BAND. House and street bases coincide on this route (SBC is inside earnings, not a separate charge), so band_position carries no information. STRATEGIC REVIEW. The September 2026 review (ring-fence or sale of the gas business, outcome by summer 2027) has no announced transaction and no price, so it does not replace the three-scenario frame; it is the main reason the 2028+ paths are judgment rather than guidance. PRICE. Regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Guidance and rate-base driven, not a trailing CAGR: FY2026 core EPS guide $1.64-1.66 (+10%), FY2027 $1.78-1.82 (+9%), then a fade as the cut capital plan slows rate-base growth. 7.0% is the base-case FY2026-FY2031 average.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR 9.1% is more than 30% above revenue 5-year CAGR 6.2%. Equity growth is inflated by external capital (2024 common issuance and the $1.6B mandatory convertible preferred), not only retained earnings, so it is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS 5-year CAGR is undefined (FY2020 GAAP EPS -$1.05) and the 3-year figure is GAAP diluted ($0.84 to $1.18). FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported and owner FCF are negative in every year FY2018-FY2025 by design of the capital program. FY2018-FY2020 are distorted by the wildfire charges, Chapter 11 and the July 2020 recapitalisation, which took the share count from 529M to 1,985M.

base.growth_note: Core EPS: FY2026 $1.65 and FY2027 $1.80 (guidance midpoints), then 8% fading to 3.5% by FY2035. The fade starts below the former 9%+ target because the FY2027 capital plan was cut $2B to $11.4B and 2028-2030 rate-base guidance is withdrawn; the 2026 authorized ROE is 9.98% on a 52% equity layer.
base.margin_note: 85% = 100% less ~10% recurring non-core cost (the GAAP-to-core gap, mostly Wildfire Fund expense and contributions) less ~5% expected wildfire disallowance. The 5% is roughly a full AB 1054/SB 254 capped disallowance (about $5.1B pre-tax for 2026 ignitions, 20% of the equity portion of electric T&D rate base) once in about twenty years.
base.capex_note: capex_pct = margin minus dividend payout on core earnings. Payout 12% in FY2026 ($0.20 on $1.65), 16% in FY2027, 20% from FY2028 per the stated target, then rising to 54% by FY2035 as growth slows and less retention is needed.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 3.0% = 17.2x the terminal dividend, about 9.3x core EPS and roughly 1.1x book: a utility whose owner ROE (~9.5%) sits just above its cost of equity is worth a little over book. The 28x cap is on the dividend flow and does not bind.

bull.growth_note: Guidance for FY2026-27, then the former 9% target is restored through FY2030 as the capital plan is reinstated on a lower cost of capital and signed large-load interconnections add rate base; fades to 4% by FY2035.
bull.margin_note: 92%: non-core costs shrink to ~6% as bankruptcy-era items roll off and wildfire reform cuts the expected disallowance to ~2%.
bull.capex_note: Payout 20% from FY2028 through FY2030, rising to 56% by FY2035.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 3.5% = 18.8x the terminal dividend, about 10.5x core EPS. The same cost of equity as base: a re-rating to peer P/E multiples would need a lower discount rate, which the house method does not grant per scenario.

bear.growth_note: FY2027 lands at the bottom of a cut guide ($1.75). A catastrophic equipment-caused fire in the 2028 season stalls per-share earnings (0% then -5%) as the capital plan is cut again and equity is raised below book to hold the capital structure; 3% thereafter on a lower authorized ROE.
bear.margin_note: 72% from FY2028: a full capped disallowance amortised against earnings, higher Wildfire Fund replenishment charges and unrecovered financing cost.
bear.capex_note: Dividend suspended FY2028-FY2030 (capex_pct equals the margin, so the flow is zero), resumed at 15% of core earnings in FY2031 and rebuilt to 40% by FY2035.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.0% / 2.5% = 15.8x the terminal dividend, about 6.3x core EPS. This is a capped-liability bear, not a repeat of 2019: the terminal value stays positive because AB 1054 holds. A fire that voids the cap (safety certification lost, or a conscious-disregard finding) is outside all three scenarios.

scenario_narratives.base: PG&E earns close to its 9.98% authorized ROE on a rate base that keeps growing, but more slowly than the pre-September plan: FY2026 and FY2027 land on guidance ($1.65, $1.80), the strategic review ends without a transformative deal, and capital spending settles near $11-12B a year, giving 7-8% per-share growth to 2030 fading to 3.5%. California's wildfire framework stays as it is (AB 1054 and SB 254 intact, no further reform), so shareholders keep paying about 10% of core earnings in non-core wildfire-fund and legacy costs and carry an expected capped disallowance worth another 5%. The dividend follows the stated policy to 20% of core earnings by 2028 and rises only as growth fades, with no new equity. Value comes out slightly above book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The legislature passes durable wildfire liability reform under the new governor, the agencies lift the holding company to investment grade, and the strategic review concludes with the capital plan reinstated, possibly funded by a gas-business sale at or above rate base. Data-centre load converts from pipeline to signed interconnections, spreading fixed costs and making 9% rate-base growth affordable to customers through 2030. Non-core leakage falls as bankruptcy-era costs roll off and the expected disallowance shrinks. The upside in this model is limited to better earnings and payout at an unchanged 9% cost of equity; the larger market upside, a re-rating toward peer multiples, would come from a lower required return and is deliberately not modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: Reform stays stalled and a PG&E line starts a catastrophic fire in the 2028 season. The CPUC finds the utility imprudent and imposes the full capped disallowance; ratings fall, the common dividend is suspended for three years as it was after 2017, the capital plan is cut again and equity is issued below book. The CPUC trims the authorized ROE at the next cost-of-capital proceeding and the Wildfire Fund needs replenishing at shareholder cost. Earnings per share stall near $1.70 and compound at only 3% thereafter. The liability cap holds, so this is a deep impairment rather than a second bankruptcy.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the equity depends on a single regulator and a single state's liability law, SB 492 stalled in September 2026, the company has caused catastrophic fires in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022, and climate trend makes the hazard worse, not better. Base 50%: FY2026-27 guidance is specific and was reaffirmed in October, and the regulatory mechanics are well established. Bull cut from 35% to 20%: it needs legislation, a ratings upgrade, a successful strategic review and data-centre conversions together, and none is in the company's control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a spread business on equity: it is worth more than book only to the extent its earned return on equity exceeds its cost of equity, and growth adds value only at that spread. PG&E's allowed ROE of about 10% against a 9% cost of equity, after deducting the wildfire-related costs that never reach shareholders, leaves a thin spread, so fair value sits near book ($15.13 diluted) in the base case and well below it if a capped wildfire disallowance is realised. The valued flow is the dividend, with payout tied to the retention that rate-base growth requires. The stock looks optically cheap on core P/E (about 8x FY2026) because the market is pricing the same wildfire tail this model carries in its bear case and haircuts; the model does not find a large margin of safety at the current price, and the 15% hurdle entry price is far below it, as is normal for a slow-growing asset discounted at 9%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: at ROE close to CoE the value is very sensitive to the rate. One point up (10%) cuts base value about 18%, one point down (8%) adds about 25%; a peer-like 8.25% would put base near $18.

A wildfire that voids the AB 1054 disallowance cap (lost safety certification or a conscious-disregard finding), or exhaustion of the Wildfire Fund and Continuation Account, is outside all three scenarios and would be a 2019-style equity event.

The FY0 core EPS of $1.50 is backed out of guidance wording, not read from a filing; the 10% non-core haircut is calibrated to the GAAP-to-core gap, part of which is non-cash amortisation of the 2020 Wildfire Fund contribution.

2028+ growth and payout are judgment: multi-year capital and rate-base guidance is withdrawn until the strategic review concludes (expected by summer 2027). A gas-business sale would change the earnings base, leverage and share count.
The no-equity-through-2030 statement predates the review's outcome; any issuance below book is directly dilutive to this valuation.
CPUC outcomes: the 2027 GRC (A.25-05-009), the Dixie/Mosquito cost-recovery decision and the next cost-of-capital reset all move earned ROE.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 11.77-19.16
data_sources.financials: PCG_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2006-Q2 2026); PCG 10-Q Q3 2026 for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, diluted share reconciliation, dividend policy, capex forecast ($12.4B 2026, $11.4B 2027), no-equity statement and the $5.1B maximum disallowance; PCG 10-K FY2025 for the 2026 cost-of-capital decision (ROE 9.98%, 52% equity)
data_sources.qualitative: PCG_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): Q3 2026 guidance (FY2026 core EPS $1.64-1.66, FY2027 $1.78-1.82), strategic review, SB 492, data-centre pipeline, credit ratings
